fact_check_rounds.label: Round 1: every profiled plant (six checkers, one per profiler batch, on the unmerged profiler files)

Round 2: line check of every High and Medium plant's opening line and bottleneck guess (72 lines, two checkers who did not write them); 7 of the 11 corrections were blank map fields whose evidence text was right: text errors 4 / 72 = 5.6%
Cross-vertical checks (state air permits, job-board dates, OSHA headcounts, profiles of OSHA top-40 entrants): rows for this vertical's plants

Base-record sample: 14 of 39 base and 8 of 61 excluded records from closure 3 and the miss verifications, 20 of the sweep's 144 rows and the coordinator's 9 ruling rows, seeded (reported separately; not a profile round)

miss_rate.note: R2 blind audit after closure 3: 5 verified misses / (31 included plants the auditors found + 5). Auditors: job postings (C) and project records, supplier awards and MBI lists (D); neither reached a dry point. Counting only auditor rows marked plant-confirmed: 4/25 = 16.0%. Against the list before closure 3: 7/36 = 19.4%. Upper bound counting 5 company-level or city-less candidates as misses: 10/41 = 24.4%. Two R1 misses (Schneider El Paso, PowerFlo Williamstown) were later excluded; the R1 figure is kept as measured.

known_limits: Neither blind audit reached a dry point in either round; the R2 upper bound is 24.4%.
The large-switchgear rule first existed only in a verifier brief written after the R1 candidate names were known; rubric R1-R6 was written down (consultation 27) before closure 3 and the R2 audit.

Closure 3 screened 1,030 OSHA and sister-site rows: 616 with no in-scope evidence are logged in ledger/audit/dc-closure3-screen-*.json rather than as excluded records (about 63 of them not read because the site was unreachable or nearly empty), and 154 rows were left as leads, many not read (59 in the second switchgear half alone).
Sister sites of the largest parents (Eaton, Siemens, ABB, Schneider, Flex, Hubbell, Legrand, Mitsubishi) were mostly screened from the OSHA record alone.
Weld process scores 0 at the nVent sites and several switchgear plants because their postings say 'weld' without naming MIG or flux-core: unknown, not absent.

City-only job postings are placed by one written site-tie test (consultation 28): nVent Houston, Vertiv Pelzer and Anderson, FTI Olathe, El Paso, Pittsboro and Opelika, Vertiv Ironton, Crusoe Arvada and BASX Redmond keep their points without confidence; Eaton Greenwood's five welder postings earn 0 because Eaton runs other buildings in Greenwood (77 High if a posting names the plant).

FTI El Paso, Pittsboro and Opelika (59 Medium, not yet operating) are credited for a city-only Journeyman Pipefitter posting; operating FTI Olathe (47) is not, because its matching posting carries the locality label 'Olathe Mechanical'. Each of the three is 35 Low if its tie fails.
Steel is not shown at some rack, cooling and switchgear plants (Vertiv Anderson's welding evidence is aluminum; Rittal Urbana and Vertiv Ironton do not state the metal).

Pre-production and not-yet-open plants are scored on what is stated (FTI Monroe, Pittsboro, Opelika and El Paso; Powell Jacintoport's prospect test is unknown); M&I Electric Beaumont (base, not profiled) has no dated source showing it operating.

Leads not yet in the ledger: an April 8, 2026 Maysteel news post says Steele Solutions acquired Maysteel (parent not updated); Forgent Dayton's two MIG postings first appear on its board 2026-09-02 (the lines use the later re-list date).
